metadata.title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning
metadata.authors: V. Mnih, A. Puigdomenech Badia, M. Mirza, A. Graves, T. Harley, T. P. Lillicrap, D. Silver, K. Kavukcuoglu

nodes.name: Reinforcement Learning Setting
nodes.statement: An agent interacts with environment $\mathcal{E}$ over discrete time steps; at time $t$ it observes state $s_t$, picks action $a_t \in \mathcal{A}$ via policy $\pi$, and receives reward $r_t$ and next state $s_{t+1}$.

nodes.name: Discounted Return
nodes.statement: $R_t = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \gamma^k r_{t+k}$ is the total accumulated return from time step $t$ with discount factor $\gamma \in (0,1]$.

nodes.name: Action-Value Function $Q^{\pi}$
nodes.statement: $Q^{\pi}(s,a) = \mathbb{E}\left[R_t \mid s_t = s, a\right]$ is the expected return for taking action $a$ in state $s$ and following policy $\pi$ thereafter.

nodes.name: Optimal Action-Value $Q^*$
nodes.statement: $Q^*(s,a) = \max_{\pi} Q^{\pi}(s,a)$ is the maximum action value for state $s$ and action $a$ achievable by any policy.

nodes.name: State-Value Function $V^{\pi}$
nodes.statement: $V^{\pi}(s) = \mathbb{E}\left[R_t \mid s_t = s\right]$, the expected return for following policy $\pi$ from state $s$.

nodes.name: Advantage Function
nodes.statement: $A(a_t,s_t) = Q(a_t,s_t) - V(s_t)$, the advantage of action $a_t$ in state $s_t$ over the average value of state $s_t$.

nodes.name: $n$-step Return
nodes.statement: The $n$-step return is $r_t + \gamma r_{t+1} + \cdots + \gamma^{n-1} r_{t+n-1} + \gamma^n \max_a Q(s_{t+n}, a)$, propagating a reward to $n$ preceding state-action pairs.

nodes.name: Forward View
nodes.statement: Computation of $n$-step returns by explicitly waiting for $n$ steps of experience before updating, as opposed to the backward view of eligibility traces.

nodes.name: Entropy Regularization Term
nodes.statement: An additional term $\beta\, H(\pi(s_t;\theta'))$ added to the policy objective, where $H$ is the entropy of the policy and $\beta$ controls its strength; it discourages premature convergence to deterministic policies.

nodes.name: Expected Return Maximization (RL Objective)
nodes.statement: Find a policy $\pi$ that maximizes the expected discounted return $\mathbb{E}[R_t]$ from each state $s_t$.

nodes.name: One-step Q-learning Loss
nodes.statement: $L_i(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}\left(r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s', a'; \theta_{i-1}) - Q(s,a;\theta_i)\right)^2$, where $s'$ is the next state.

nodes.name: REINFORCE Policy Gradient with Baseline
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{\theta} \log\pi(a_t|s_t;\theta)\, (R_t - b_t(s_t))$, where $b_t(s_t) \approx V^{\pi}(s_t)$ is a learned baseline.

nodes.name: A3C Policy Gradient with Entropy Regularization
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{\theta'} \log\pi(a_t|s_t;\theta')\, (R_t - V(s_t;\theta_v)) + \beta\, \nabla_{\theta'} H(\pi(s_t;\theta'))$.

nodes.name: A3C Advantage Estimator
nodes.statement: $A(s_t,a_t;\theta,\theta_v) = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \gamma^i r_{t+i} + \gamma^k V(s_{t+k};\theta_v) - V(s_t;\theta_v)$, with $k$ upper-bounded by $t_{max}$.

nodes.name: Non-centered RMSProp Update
nodes.statement: $g = \alpha g + (1-\alpha)\Delta\theta^2$ and $\theta \gets \theta - \eta\, \frac{\Delta\theta}{\sqrt{g+\epsilon}}$, with all operations elementwise.

nodes.name: Asynchronous one-step Q-learning
nodes.statement: Multi-threaded actor-learner variant of Q-learning: each thread interacts with its own environment copy, computes Q-learning gradients, and asynchronously updates a shared parameter vector $\theta$ via Hogwild!-style updates.
input: Global shared parameters $\theta$, target network $\theta^-$, counter $T=0$

nodes.name: Asynchronous one-step Sarsa
nodes.statement: Same as Asynchronous one-step Q-learning except the target value is $r + \gamma Q(s', a'; \theta^-)$ where $a'$ is the action actually taken in $s'$ (on-policy target).
input: Global shared parameters $\theta$, target network $\theta^-$, counter $T$

nodes.name: Asynchronous $n$-step Q-learning
nodes.statement: Forward-view multi-step Q-learning: each thread rolls out up to $t_{max}$ steps, then accumulates $n$-step Q-learning gradients for each visited state-action pair before performing one asynchronous update.
input: Rollout length $t_{max}$, target update interval $I_{target}$, max steps $T_{max}$

nodes.name: Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (A3C)
nodes.statement: Forward-view actor-critic that maintains a policy $\pi(a_t|s_t;\theta)$ and value function $V(s_t;\theta_v)$, updates both with the $n$-step advantage estimator, and uses entropy regularization to encourage exploration.
input: Rollout length $t_{max}$, entropy weight $\beta$, max steps $T_{max}$
output: Trained policy parameters $\theta$ and value parameters $\theta_v$

nodes.name: Asynchronous Momentum SGD (Hogwild!-style)
nodes.statement: Each thread $i$ independently applies momentum SGD with its own momentum vector: $m_i = \alpha m_i + (1-\alpha) \Delta\theta_i$ then $\theta \gets \theta - \eta m_i$ on the shared $\theta$ without locks.

nodes.name: Shared RMSProp
nodes.statement: RMSProp variant where the moving average of squared gradients $g$ is shared across threads and updated asynchronously without locking, reducing memory and improving robustness vs per-thread RMSProp.

nodes.name: DQN
nodes.statement: Deep Q-Network using experience replay and a slowly-updated target network to stabilize off-policy Q-learning with deep neural function approximators.

nodes.name: Gorila (General Reinforcement Learning Architecture)
nodes.statement: Massively distributed asynchronous DQN: separate actor processes with local replay memories send DQN gradients to a central parameter server (e.g., 130 machines), reaching DQN-level scores >20x faster.

nodes.name: REINFORCE
nodes.statement: Policy-gradient algorithm that updates $\theta$ in the direction $\nabla_{\theta} \log\pi(a_t|s_t;\theta) R_t$, an unbiased estimate of $\nabla_{\theta} \mathbb{E}[R_t]$.

nodes.name: Atari 2600 Learning-Speed Comparison
nodes.statement: On five Atari games (Beamrider, Breakout, Pong, Q*bert, Space Invaders), the four asynchronous methods (using 16 CPU cores) match or beat DQN trained on a K40 GPU; A3C performs best.

nodes.name: A3C on 57 Atari Games
nodes.statement: A3C trained for 4 days on 16 CPU cores improves the state-of-the-art mean and median human-normalized scores on 57 Atari games, with hyperparameters tuned on six games (Beamrider, Breakout, Pong, Q*bert, Seaquest, Space Invaders).

nodes.name: TORCS Car Racing
nodes.statement: On the TORCS 3D car-racing simulator (slow/fast car, with/without bots) using only RGB visual input, A3C reaches roughly 75-90% of human tester score in about 12 hours of training.

nodes.name: MuJoCo Continuous Control
nodes.statement: Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic with a Gaussian policy ($\mu$ from linear layer, $\sigma^2$ from SoftPlus) solves rigid-body manipulation and locomotion tasks from physical state or pixels in under 24 hours of CPU training.

nodes.name: Labyrinth Random-Maze Navigation
nodes.statement: An A3C LSTM agent trained on $84\times 84$ RGB inputs learns to find apples (+1) and portals (+10) in randomly generated 3D mazes, achieving an average score of around 50.

nodes.name: Scalability vs Number of Threads
nodes.statement: On seven Atari games, training-time speedups with $\{1,2,4,8,16\}$ threads reach $\{1.0,3.0,6.3,13.3,24.1\}$ for 1-step Q (superlinear) and $\{1.0,2.1,3.7,6.9,12.5\}$ for A3C; one-step methods exhibit superlinear scaling attributed to bias reduction from parallel actors.

nodes.name: Robustness to Learning Rate
nodes.statement: Across 50 random learning rates and initializations on five Atari games, A3C and the other three asynchronous methods exhibit a wide range of learning rates that yield good scores with virtually no diverging runs.

nodes.name: Optimization-Method Comparison
nodes.statement: Comparison of Momentum SGD, RMSProp (per-thread), and Shared RMSProp on Async $n$-step Q and A3C across four Atari games (Breakout, Beamrider, Seaquest, Space Invaders); Shared RMSProp is the most robust to learning-rate and initialization choices.

nodes.name: Parallel Actors Decorrelate Updates
nodes.statement: Running multiple actor-learners in parallel with different exploration policies decorrelates the data stream and stabilizes online updates, removing the need for experience replay and enabling on-policy methods like Sarsa and actor-critic with deep nets.

nodes.name: Forward vs Backward View for $n$-step Methods
nodes.statement: We use the forward view (explicit $n$-step returns as targets) instead of eligibility-trace backward view because it is easier to combine with momentum-based optimization and backpropagation through time on neural networks.

nodes.name: Shared Network for Policy and Value
nodes.statement: In practice, A3C uses a single convolutional network with one softmax output for $\pi(a_t|s_t;\theta)$ and one linear output for $V(s_t;\theta_v)$, sharing all non-output layers.

nodes.name: Superlinear Speedup of One-step Methods
nodes.statement: Asynchronous one-step Q-learning and Sarsa exhibit superlinear training-time speedups in the number of threads, attributed to multiple parallel actors reducing the bias of one-step bootstrapped targets.

nodes.name: Initialize thread-local and shared state
nodes.statement: Set thread step counter $t \gets 0$, target weights $\theta^- \gets \theta$, gradients $d\theta \gets 0$, and obtain initial state $s$.

nodes.name: Outer loop: act, observe, accumulate
nodes.statement: Repeat: take action $a$ via $\epsilon$-greedy on $Q(s,a;\theta)$, observe $r$ and $s'$; compute target $y = r$ if $s'$ terminal else $r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a';\theta^-)$; accumulate $d\theta \gets d\theta + \partial(y - Q(s,a;\theta))^2 / \partial\theta$; set $s \gets s'$ and increment $T,t$.

nodes.name: Periodic target-network sync
nodes.statement: If $T \bmod I_{target} == 0$, set $\theta^- \gets \theta$ to refresh the slowly-updated target network.

nodes.name: Periodic asynchronous parameter update
nodes.statement: If $t \bmod I_{AsyncUpdate} == 0$ or $s$ is terminal, perform asynchronous (Hogwild!-style) update of shared $\theta$ using $d\theta$, then clear $d\theta \gets 0$.

nodes.name: Termination
nodes.statement: Continue until global counter exceeds $T_{max}$, then return.

nodes.name: Initialize and synchronize parameters
nodes.statement: Set thread step counter $t \gets 1$, $\theta^- \gets \theta$, $\theta' = \theta$, $d\theta \gets 0$.

nodes.name: Roll out up to $t_{max}$ steps
nodes.statement: From $t_{start}=t$, repeatedly take $a_t$ via $\epsilon$-greedy on $Q(s_t,a;\theta')$, observe $r_t$ and $s_{t+1}$, increment $t$ and $T$, until $s_t$ terminal or $t - t_{start} == t_{max}$.

nodes.name: Bootstrap return $R$
nodes.statement: Set $R = 0$ if $s_t$ terminal, else $R = \max_a Q(s_t, a; \theta^-)$.

nodes.name: Backward accumulate $n$-step gradients
nodes.statement: For $i \in \{t-1, \ldots, t_{start}\}$: $R \gets r_i + \gamma R$; $d\theta \gets d\theta + \partial(R - Q(s_i,a_i;\theta'))^2 / \partial\theta'$.

nodes.name: Async update and target sync
nodes.statement: Perform asynchronous update of shared $\theta$ using $d\theta$; if $T \bmod I_{target} == 0$, set $\theta^- \gets \theta$. Repeat outer loop until $T > T_{max}$.

nodes.name: Reset gradients and synchronize parameters
nodes.statement: Set $d\theta \gets 0$, $d\theta_v \gets 0$; synchronize $\theta' = \theta$ and $\theta'_v = \theta_v$.

nodes.name: Roll out trajectory of length up to $t_{max}$
nodes.statement: From $t_{start}=t$, sample $a_t \sim \pi(a_t|s_t;\theta')$, observe $r_t$, $s_{t+1}$, increment $t$ and $T$ until $s_t$ terminal or $t - t_{start} == t_{max}$.

nodes.name: Bootstrap value $R$
nodes.statement: Set $R = 0$ if $s_t$ terminal, else $R = V(s_t, \theta'_v)$ as bootstrap from the last state.

nodes.name: Backward accumulate policy and value gradients
nodes.statement: For $i \in \{t-1, \ldots, t_{start}\}$: $R \gets r_i + \gamma R$; $d\theta \gets d\theta + \nabla_{\theta'} \log\pi(a_i|s_i;\theta')(R - V(s_i;\theta'_v))$; $d\theta_v \gets d\theta_v + \partial(R - V(s_i;\theta'_v))^2 / \partial\theta'_v$.

nodes.name: Asynchronous update of $\theta$ and $\theta_v$
nodes.statement: Perform asynchronous (Hogwild!-style) update of shared $\theta$ using $d\theta$ and of $\theta_v$ using $d\theta_v$; repeat outer loop until $T > T_{max}$.
